title: Interim toward C:open-ended: in the continuous-trait fed vortices, a kind-specific waste (eaters release a diffusing waste that holds back vortices of a similar trait) makes the trait distribution branch and keeps new classes taking the plurality: 8 distinct dominant classes with 4-5 first-time dominants after t=3000 on 2/2 seeds, against 2 classes and 0-1 in the kind-blind-waste twin with the same draws
summary: World 20261027T1245-c58-vortex-waste-novelty/world.py: the continuous-trait fed vortices (20261027T1230-c58-vortex-trait-climb, whole-vortex trait-blind mutation +-0.4 every 50 t) plus a waste W released by eating (pw 0.25, Dw 1, decay 0.002) that carries the eater's trait; the gain is k(1 + 0.25 (1 - W/(1+W) G)), G = exp(-(theta - theta_W)^2/(2 0.4^2)). The kind-blind twin has G = 1, so its gain does not depend on theta: it is the matched neutral twin with the same waste ecology and the same mutation draws. trait.py + novelty.py, seeds 1-2, T=6000: kind-specific waste: distinct dominant classes 8/8, first-time dominants after t=3000 4/5, classes ever held by >= 3 vortices 12/10, class range at the end -7..3 and -4..4 (two branches on seed 1, novelty_s1s2.png); kind-blind twin: 2/2, 1/0, 6/5, -5..2 and -2..3; the no-waste neutral twin (eps 0): 2/1, 1/0. Daughters keep the parent's class at 58/71 and 102/124 splits (kind-blind 220/259, 190/220).

finding.operator: kind-specific waste (negative frequency dependence carried by a diffusing, decaying field that records the eater's trait)
finding.control: kind-blind waste twin (sw 0: gain independent of the trait, same ecology and mutation draws), seeds 1 2
finding.result: distinct dominant classes 8/8 vs 2/2; first-time dominants after t=3000 4/5 vs 1/0; classes ever held by >= 3 vortices 12/10 vs 6/5

limits: Interim: two seeds, T=6000, 128^2, one parameter point, no dt/2 or grid test; long runs (T=12000) are running to test whether new classes keep coming or the count saturates. The fitness effect is written: the waste records the eater's trait and the gain reads the trait, which builds in negative frequency dependence (rare classes are favoured), so turnover is expected from the rule; what the run shows is that the vortices' own heredity carries it (copying and mutation never read the trait). The trait is one scalar: classes are bins of width 0.4 on a line, and 'new' means a bin not dominant before, so a long random walk would also visit new bins; the twins bound that. Returns to an earlier dominant class are frequent (4 and 7), so part of the turnover is cycling. Heredity is weaker in this arm (daughter class fidelity 82%, within-vortex spread median 0.04-0.05 vs 0.01): diverse traits fuse. Branching is seen on seed 1 (two clusters), less clearly on seed 2.
